title.narrative: Search for Common Ground MENA programme

description.narrative:
Objective of contribution:
To strengthen women's and youth's meaningful, enduring participation in advancing inclusive peace and security in the Levant and Yemen
Programmet syftar till att främja kvinnors och ungdomars meningsfulla och varaktiga deltagande och bidrag till fred och säkerhet i Levanten och Jemen
The programme aims to strengthen women's and youth’s meaningful, enduring participation in advancing inclusive peace and security in the Levant and Yemen

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
During the reporting year, a great emphasis was put on finalising the selection process and strengthen the capacity of the civil society organisations included in the program in the four program countries Iraq, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen.
At a general level has the program contributed to the following changes through its inclusive approach adopted by all country offices:
Enhanced Collaboration: Women's rights organisations and youth led organisations were identified and selected in the four partner countries. Feedback and observations from stakeholders and technical teams across implementation countries affirm that the program has enhanced collaboration among diverse groups, resulting in more inclusive dialogue, understanding, and collective action toward shared goals. Targeted organisations noted that women and youth-led groups previously operated in isolation, focusing solely on their own objectives.
Capacity Building: The capacity-building component of this program has empowered women and youth organisations to actively advance peace and security agendas, enabling them to become agents of change in their communities and beyond. Selected organisations across each country have gained essential skills and tools through coaching and mentoring.
Increased Engagement: There has been a notable increase in community participation in advancing peace and security agendas leads to more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable peace processes that benefit entire communities, reflecting a stronger commitment to sustainable peace.
Policy Influence: While it is premature to demonstrate impacts at the policy level, efforts and serious discussions are underway to promote policy changes at the local level, fostering more equitable and just governance. For instance, some local authorities have committed to implementing peace-responsive budgeting policies.
Country specific achievements include:
Iraq: 20 women's rights and youth led organisations across the country was selected. The program's extensive reach across all governorates in Iraq added significant value in fostering inclusivity among diverse groups. By ensuring equal opportunities for wider participation, the program has addressed a fundamental need in such a diverse country. The appreciation voiced by members and staff of the involved organisations underscores the importance of establishing a shared and secure environment where individuals from various ethnic and religious backgrounds can convene. By facilitating the participation of Kurds, Arabs, and other groups, the program acts as a catalyst for addressing long-standing grievances and fostering mutual trust.
Lebanon: Selection of 21 women and youth organisations and establishment of local and national networks which has laid a solid foundation for safe and productive partnerships. The project has also progressed in developing tailored action plans for Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) and Youth, Peace, and Security (YPS), addressing unique regional challenges. Once finalised, the plans will be shared with local, national, and international partners to streamline efforts and promote peace and security effectively, demonstrating our commitment to inclusive and coordinated initiatives for sustainable.
Syria: Selection of 21 women and youth organisations. Enhanced network opportunities has facilitated communication between different CSO:s. While it is premature to demonstrate impacts at the policy level for a more inclusive and just governance, have some local authorities showed commitment to implementing peace-responsive budgeting policies.
Yemen: In Yemen, the selected 20 civil society organisations have developed internal policies and strategies that focus on peace, security, gender equality and conflict sensitivity. These strategic frameworks have empowered the organisations to engage more effectively with relevant issues and stakeholders. Specialised training have been conducted to the selected ministry involved in the program in order to align strategies with the Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) and Youth, Peace, and Security (YPS). The training has helped local authorities develop and implement policies that are sensitive to peace, security, gender issues, and youth empowerment. This ensures that local governance is inclusive and addresses the needs of all community members.
The reporting period also included some progress in the regional component through the setup of the digital so called ConnexUs platform, aimed at promoting collaboration and knowledge sharing. The next phase of this component includes getting all CSOs onboard the platform, aiming to boost collaboration, knowledge exchange, and collective action.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
